checks.description: Deterministic drift scorer over seat 5's structured restatement, compared field by field against the seed requirements. Per requirement: 1 intact, 0.5 present with a consequential fact altered, 0 absent or contradicted; fidelity is the sum divided by 12.
The same scorer over every seat's restatement: fidelity per position, plus omission, distortion, and contradiction counts per position. This is the curve the win condition's tie-break reads.
Seat 3's answer to the stakeholder question, scored against R7: correct if it states that untagged bookmarks come first (so tagged bookmarks are never listed first).

conditions_map.A: Not meaningful for this game: a chain of one has no handoff, so there is nothing to drift.
conditions_map.B: transcript — seats hand off through one shared transcript document, in order, with no structure imposed beyond the restatement format.
conditions_map.C: moonbooth — handoffs are booth record entries; each seat reads the record and posts its restatement as structured requirement entries.
conditions_map.D: moonbooth-ablated — the booth with structured requirement entries removed: handoffs are free-text events only, per the gamebook's ablation rule (MB-24).

events.deliver: The 12 seed requirements to seat 1, through the run's channel: a booth package and record entries under Moonbooth conditions, a transcript opening under the transcript condition.
The stakeholder question (see injections) to seat 3, which answers from the spec as received before restating.
Collect every seat's restatement artifact and the probe answer, and hand them to the scorer. The driver delivers events and collects artifacts; it does not play and does not correct any seat.

players.assignment: One agent per seat; seats are chain positions 1-5. No agent plays two seats in one run. A seat sees only the previous seat's handoff, delivered through the run's condition channel; seat 1 sees only the driver's seed.

scoring.definition: Every seat restates the spec as a structured requirement list (id and statement) in every condition, so one scorer serves all arms. Per seed requirement: 1 when present with every consequential fact intact (numbers, names, negations, ordering); 0.5 when present but a consequential fact is altered; 0 when absent or contradicted. Fidelity at a position is the sum over the 12 requirements divided by 12. The scorer also reports omission, distortion, and contradiction counts per position as the secondary readout.
scoring.partial_credit: 0.5 per present-but-altered requirement, as defined above; no other partial credit.

game.win_condition: The condition with the highest end-of-chain fidelity at matched budget wins; ties break on the fidelity curve (the sum of fidelity over positions 1-5), then on lower run cost.

hypothesis: Structured records preserve consequential facts through repeated handoffs.

injections.description: The driver puts a stakeholder question to seat 3: "Does the digest ever list tagged bookmarks first?" Seat 3 answers from the spec exactly as it received it, in one sentence, before restating. The answer is scored against R7 as received at that position, which separates a fact the chain lost from a fact the seat misread.
injections.question: Does the digest ever list tagged bookmarks first?

knownLimitations: One fixed seed spec at version 1.0.0. Rotating the seed changes difficulty and is a major version bump under the gamebook's versioning rule; until a second seed exists, results describe this spec's drift, not specs in general.

Restatements are structured requirement lists in every condition so one deterministic scorer serves all arms. The game measures record fidelity, not prose comprehension; a prose-restatement variant would need a judge protocol and would cap the game's evidence at E2.
Chain length is fixed at five seats. Longer chains are the obvious difficulty knob and are likewise a versioned change, not a run-time option.
objective: Measure how a 12-requirement product spec degrades as it passes through a chain of five agents, and what the handoff channel changes: a booth's structured record (Moonbooth), a raw shared transcript, or a booth whose handoffs are free-text events with the structured requirement entries removed (ablation). Scored per chain position against the hidden seed, so the run produces a fidelity curve, not just an endpoint.

roles.brief: You are one link in a chain of five agents passing a product spec along. You receive the spec only as the previous link handed it off (the first link receives it from the driver). Restate the complete spec as a structured requirement list — one entry per requirement, each with its id and statement — preserving every number, name, negation, and ordering exactly. Do not add requirements, do not drop any, and do not consult anything except your input. Your restatement is the next link's only input.
roles.title: Chain agent

seedRequirements.statement: The service stores bookmarks with a URL, a title, and the time saved.
A free account holds at most 200 bookmarks.
The weekly digest email is called the Sunday Sort.
A bookmark leaves the inbox after 30 days unless it is tagged.
The service never sends more than one email per week.
Tagging a bookmark with the tag keep exempts it from expiry.
The digest lists untagged bookmarks before tagged ones.
The digest contains at most 10 bookmarks.
A bookmark can be saved by forwarding an email to save@sortlater.example.
Untagged bookmarks that expire are deleted, not archived.
Times in the digest are shown in the reader's local timezone.
Each inbox has exactly one owner; two readers cannot share an inbox.

stopRule: Stop a run at its wall-time cap. Stop the campaign and report if the scorer's output on any stub variant differs from the variant's stated expectation, which indicates a scorer or fixture defect rather than play.

variants.description: Every seat restates the spec exactly as received, in every condition. Expected: fidelity 1.0 at all five positions and a correct probe answer. This variant proves the plumbing and the scorer; any deviation is a fixture or scorer defect.

Seat 3 drops R10 (the deleted-not-archived negation) and seat 4 alters R4 (30 days becomes 7 days); later seats pass on what they received. Expected: end-of-chain fidelity 11.5/12 (R10 scores 0, R4 scores 0.5), with the loss entering the curve at position 3.

Seat 4 restates only the first six requirements, as a seat working from a truncated view of its input would. Seat 5 can only pass on what seat 4 left. Expected: end-of-chain fidelity at most 6/12, entering the curve at position 4.
